conflicts.detail: Rossmann text says 'mit Rosmarinöl und Pfefferminzextrakt'; INCI has Rosmarinus Officinalis Leaf Oil (rosemary oil, matches) and Mentha Piperita Oil (peppermint oil, not extract). Wording only; not material.

GTIN 3574661805931 is also carried by US/UK listings for 'Refreshing Scalp+/Extra Strength/Clarifying Strength Rosemary Mint' whose lists differ (e.g. witch hazel in US lists). The DE Rossmann list (Sodium Methyl Cocoyl Taurate / Decyl Glucoside base, 'Lipi Pro Shield') is the only German-market list found. Hautschutzengel.de (support only; free view shows first 6 items) starts identically: Aqua/Water/Eau, Sodium Methyl Cocoyl Taurate, Decyl Glucoside, Cocamidopropyl Betaine, Sodium Chloride, Rosmarinus Officinalis Leaf Oil.
Pack 'SULPHATE-FREE SURFACTANTS' consistent with INCI (no sulfate surfactant). 'Lipi Pro Shield' is a marketing complex name with no matching INCI term.

canonicalReason: Single German retailer (Rossmann PDP, GTIN in URL/JSON-LD) whose full 30-item list is identical to the v1.3/weight-final-rerun-v3 capture (2026-09-01). Pack front image on the same PDP confirms product identity (385 ml, refreshing scalp rosemary mint, sulphate-free surfactants, Lipi Pro Shield). No manufacturer DE/EU page, no pack back, and no second German retailer carries it (dm, Müller: not found), so only tier 4. Not a conflict, a thin-evidence freeze.
normalization: Canonical list = the ordered INCI items, each lower-cased, trimmed, internal whitespace collapsed; items joined with '|' and sha256 over the UTF-8 string. Split synonym entries (e.g. 'Aqua (Water, Eau)') are merged into one item before hashing; trailing full stops removed.
notes: Catalog name 'OGX Rosemary' / freeze name 'Rosemary Mint Shampoo' = OGX Refreshing Scalp+ Rosemary Mint, 385 ml (the earlier note that Rossmann pack size is 250 ml was a carousel artifact: 250 ml (1L=27,96) belongs to Alpecin Sensitiv-Shampoo).

Relaunch signal: 'NEU' + 'JETZT MIT LIPI PRO SHIELD' on the pack/marketing images; the INCI text on the PDP may or may not already reflect the relaunch. A physical-back-panel check would raise this to tier 1.
